newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rate cuts alone not enough for Australia - Fischer.
newsitem.headline: Rate cuts alone not enough for Australia - Fischer.

text.p: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Monday that the five cuts in the official cash rate since mid-1996 were not enough to significantly boost job creation and the economy.
"That alone is not going fire up comprehensively jobs and the economy," Fischer told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Speaking on the eve of a special cabinet meeting to consider measures to boost employment, Fischer said the government needed to use lateral thinking to boost exports.
Fischer did not detail what measures cabinet would consider.
He said, however, that no major decisions would be taken while Prime Minister John Howard remained at home recovering from a bout of pneumonia.
"There will be preliminary decisions and continuing processing of all government matters," Fischer said.
Fischer said he could not say when Howard would return to work, but that he appeared much stronger.
"His voice sounded a whole lot stronger," he said.
